Solution Design Document: E-Commerce Platform Modernization

1. OVERVIEW

This document outlines the architecture for modernizing our legacy e-commerce platform. The new system will handle 10,000 concurrent users and process 1 million transactions per day.

2. ARCHITECTURE

2.1 System Architecture

The system uses a monolithic architecture with a single PostgreSQL database. All application logic runs in a single Java application server.

Components:
- Web Application (Java Spring Boot)
- Database (PostgreSQL 12)
- File Storage (Local filesystem)
- Cache (In-memory HashMap)

2.2 Data Flow

1. User requests hit the application server directly
2. Application queries the database for every request
3. Files are stored on the application server's local disk
4. Session data is stored in the database

3. DATABASE DESIGN

Single PostgreSQL instance handles:
- User data
- Product catalog
- Orders and transactions
- Session storage
- Audit logs

All tables are in a single database with no partitioning or sharding strategy.

4. SECURITY

4.1 Authentication
- Username and password stored in database
- Passwords are MD5 hashed
- No multi-factor authentication
- Session tokens stored in cookies without HttpOnly flag

4.2 Authorization
- Role-based access control implemented in application code
- Admin credentials hardcoded in configuration file

4.3 Data Protection
- Database connections use plain text (no SSL)
- API endpoints use HTTP (no HTTPS)
- Credit card data stored in database without encryption

5. DEPLOYMENT

5.1 Infrastructure
- Single EC2 instance (t2.large)
- No load balancer
- No auto-scaling
- Manual deployment process

5.2 Monitoring
- Basic CloudWatch metrics
- No application-level monitoring
- No distributed tracing
- Logs stored locally on server

6. DISASTER RECOVERY

- Database backups run weekly
- No backup testing process
- No documented recovery procedures
- RTO: Unknown, RPO: 7 days

7. SCALABILITY PLAN

Current plan is to upgrade to a larger EC2 instance (vertical scaling) when performance degrades.

8. DEPENDENCIES

- Payment processing via third-party API (no fallback)
- Email service (single provider, no retry logic)
- External inventory system (synchronous calls)

9. FUTURE CONSIDERATIONS

- May need to add caching "at some point"
- Consider microservices "if we grow"
- Look into Kubernetes "eventually"
